chunks.arabic_text: رَوَى يُونُسُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ :

translations.en: Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

chunks.arabic_text: فِي رَجُلٍ مَاتَ وَتَرَكَ عَبْدًا فَشَهِدَ بَعْضُ وُلْدِهِ أَنَّ أَبَاهُ أَعْتَقَهُ

translations.en: Regarding a man who died and left behind a slave, and some of his children testified that their father had freed him.

chunks.arabic_text: فَقَالَ تَجُوزُ عَلَيْهِ شَهَادَتُهُ وَلَا يُغْرَمُ وَيُسْتَسْعَى الْغُلَامُ فِيمَا كَانَ لِغَيْرِهِ مِنَ الْوَرَثَةِ

translations.en: So he عليه السلام said: "His testimony is accepted against him, and he is not made financially liable; and the غلام is to work to satisfy what belonged to the other heirs."

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a case in which one heir acknowledges that a deceased father had freed a slave. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the heir's testimony is accepted with respect to his own share, while the slave must compensate the shares of the other heirs. The report concerns inheritance, testimony, and the financial rights of co-heirs.
en.seo_question: If one heir testifies that a deceased man had freed his slave, is that testimony accepted and what happens to the rights of the other heirs?

key_terms.عَبْدًا: a slave left behind as part of the deceased's estate
key_terms.شَهَادَتُهُ: his testimony or legal witness statement
key_terms.يُغْرَمُ: he is not made to pay compensation personally
key_terms.يُسْتَسْعَى: he is required to work and earn toward compensation
key_terms.الْوَرَثَةِ: the heirs entitled to shares of the estate
